facts.statement: The holotype of Gnatusuchus is a nearly complete skull (MUSM 990) found in the Iquitos area of Peru, accompanied by three partial mandible specimens.
facts.quote: Among the fossils recovered from the Iquitos localities is the holotype of Gnatusuchus, MUSM 990, a nearly complete skull, as well as 3 referred specimens consisting of a right and two partial left mandibles.

facts.statement: The genus name Gnatusuchus combines the Quechua word for 'small nose' and the Greek word for 'crocodile'.
facts.quote: The name Gnatusuchus is a combination of the Quechua word "Ñatu", meaning small nose, and the Greek "Souchos" for crocodile.

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus lived approximately 13 million years ago in the Pebas mega-wetlands, a vast system covering over one million square kilometers in modern-day Peru.
facts.quote: Gnatusuchus lived about 13 million years ago (Ma) in a large wetland system called the Pebas mega-wetlands that covered over one million square kilometers of what is now the Amazon Basin

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus had highly reduced dentition with only 14 upper teeth and 11 lower teeth, far fewer than the 18 to 20 found in other blunt-snouted caimans.
facts.quote: Gnatusuchus has highly reduced dentition compared to other blunt-snouted caimans, which typically possess 18 to 20 tooth alveoli, whereas Gnatusuchus has 14 teeth spread over the premaxilla and maxilla and 11 dentary teeth.

facts.statement: The front teeth of Gnatusuchus were long, peg-like, and procumbent, showing signs of wear on their tips.
facts.quote: The anterior most teeth are long and peg-like with blunt crowns. They are procumbent and shown apical wear.

facts.statement: The rear teeth of Gnatusuchus were globular in shape with a distinct neck.
facts.quote: The posterior teeth meanwhile are globular shaped with a distinct neck.

facts.statement: Based on skull measurements, researchers estimate Gnatusuchus reached a total body length between 148.9 and 167.7 centimeters.
facts.quote: Based on the size of the skull material Salas-Gismondi et al. estimate a total body length of 148.9 to 167.7 cm depending on the proportions used for the calculation.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that Gnatusuchus used its front teeth to shovel food while crushing bivalve shells with its tightly packed rear teeth.
facts.quote: Salas-Gismondi et al. hypothesize that Gnatusuchus used its jaw and procumbent teeth to "shovel" while crushing shells with the tightly packed posterior teeth.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Gnatusuchus as the most basal member of the Caimaninae subfamily.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis published alongside its initial description placed Gnatusuchus as the most basal member of the clade Caimaninae.

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus is classified within the family Alligatoridae.
facts.quote: familia: Alligatoridae

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus belongs to the subfamily Caimaninae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Caimaninae

facts.statement: The youngest fossil records of Gnatusuchus come from the Nueva Unión area south of Iquitos, Peru.
facts.quote: The youngest records of Gnatusuchus were found in the Nueva Unión area south of Iquitos

facts.statement: It is noted that Gnatusuchus has not been found in the Urumaco or Solimões formations where other durophagous caimans persisted after the Pebas wetlands declined.
facts.quote: However Gnatusuchus itself has not been found in either formation.

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus pebasensis was named in 2015 based on a nearly complete skull and several jaws found in the Pebas Formation near Iquitos in Peru.
facts.quote: G. pebasensis fue nombrado en 2015 basándose en un cráneo casi completo y varias mandíbulas halladas en la Formación Pebas cerca de Iquitos en Perú.

facts.statement: The genus name comes from the Quechua word ñatu, meaning "small-nosed", while the species name refers to the Amazonian city of Pebas.
facts.quote: El nombre del género proviene de la palabra quechua ñatu que significa "de nariz pequeña" mientras que el nombre de la especie se refiere a la ciudad amazónica llamada Pebas.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis published with its original scientific description places Gnatusuchus as the most basal member of the Caimaninae clade.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético publicado junto con su descripción científica original sitúa a Gnatusuchus como el miembro más basal del clado Caimaninae.

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus belongs to the parent group Caimaninae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Caimaninae

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus is a member of the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gnatusuchus is Gnatusuchus pebasensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Gnatusuchus pebasensis

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus lived during the Langhian to Serravallian stages, from 15.98 to 11.63 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Langhian to Serravallian (15.98 to 11.63 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gnatusuchus lived alongside six other crocodilian species, including two other caimans with crushing dentitions: Kuttanacaiman iquitosensis and Caiman wannlangstoni.
facts.quote: Vivió junto a otras seis especies de crocodilianos, incluyendo a otros dos caimanes con dentaduras para tritutar: Kuttanacaiman iquitosensis y Caiman wannlangstoni.

facts.statement: Research suggests that specialized crushing dentition was an ancestral trait in Caimaninae, as basal members like Kuttanacaiman and Globidentosuchus also possessed this feature.
facts.quote: Se encontró además que los dos otros caimaninos con dentaduras especializadas en triturar, Kuttanacaiman y Globidentosuchus, también son caimaninos basales, lo que sugiere que la dentadura especializada era un rasgo ancestral en este grupo.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the re-emergence of crushing dentition in derived species like Caiman wannlangstoni represents a convergent evolution rather than a retention of the ancestral trait.
facts.quote: Los caimaninos posteriores, incluyendo a la mayoría de especies modernas, tienen dentaduras más generalistas, aunque algunas pocas especies derivadas como C. wannlangstoni parecen haber readquirido convergentemente la dentadura para triturar.

rejected.statement: Gnatusuchus possessed an exceptionally short and rounded snout with a length-breadth index of 1.55.
rejected.quote: Gnatusuchus has a exceptionally short and rounded snout with a length-breadth index of 1.55
